newsitem.title: INDIA: TEXT - India statement on SAIL plans.
newsitem.headline: TEXT - India statement on SAIL plans.

text.p: Following is the text of the statement by the Indian government on Thursday on state-run Steel Authority of India's (SAIL) expansion and modernisation plans during the ninth five-year plan.

SAIL's modernisation programme is almost complete in Durgapur. At Rourkela and Bokaro, the work is progressing satisfactorily. It plans to add new facilities at Bhilai which is considered to be the best steel plant in the country in terms of blast furnace and labour productivity.

Since 1986, SAIL has spent over 200 billion rupees on modernisation and update of its plants. It plans to invest another approximately 150 billion rupees on update, addition, modification and replacement (AMR) schemes during the ninth plan.
With the completion of all modernisation programmes, the cost of production at SAIL plants will decline from the base price taken before the commencement of the modernisation programmes.
For instance in Rourkela, the cost of production will come down by about 1,100 rupees per tonne. The yield of saleable steel from liquid steel will improve substantially.
In Durgapur, the yield of saleable steel from liquid steel will go up from 75.1 percent to 84.5 percent. In addition, there will be an impressive rise in manpower productivity.

In Durgapur and Rourkela, it will more than double. Blast furnace productivity will increase from 0.7 tonne per cubic metre per hour (T/M3/H) to 1.04 T/M3/H in Durgapur and from 0.76 T/M3/H to 1.13 T/M3/H in Rourkela.

The cost of energy will plummet due to reduction in coke rate from 201 kg per tonne of hot metal (kg/thm) to 653 kg/thm in Durgapur and from 811 kg/thm to 700 kg/thm in Rourkela. There will also be a sharp decline in specific energy consumption.
At Durgapur, the modernised units have been commissioned and are in the process of stabilisation.
The blast furnace number 4, which is being reconstructed, is likely to be ready for commissioning by the end of the year with a useful volume of 1,800 cu.m and a slag granulation plant.
Durgapur Steel Plant, which has been a traditionally loss making unit, ended 1995/96 with a cash profit and is likely to finish the current financial year with a net profit.
With the completion of the modernisation programme, the capacity of the plant will go up to 1.87 million tonnes of crude steel from the earlier operating capacity of 0.8 million tonnes per annum.
Rourkela's two-phased modernisation programme is proceeding as per schedule and the entire work is expected to be completed soon.

The phase-I plan was commissioned in March, 1994 and the benefits envisaged from the phase-I are accruing progressively from the current financial year. The work on the phase-II modernisation, which is being executed in 20 main packages, is going on in full swing.

Some of the modernised units like BOF, Sintar Plant-II, Slab Casting Shop No.I and II, Plate Mill Reheating Furnace were commissioned in November. After update, the capacity of RSP will go up to 1.9 million tonnes of crude steel per annum from the present 1.4 million tonnes.

The modernisation programme of Bokaro Steel Plant will enhance its crude steel capacity from four million tonnes to 4.36 million tonnes. With Government approval accorded in July 1993, the programme will be completed by July 1997.

The plan of Bokaro envisages reconstruction of the existing Steel Melting Shop no.2 to increase its liquid steel capacity from 1.84 million tonnes to 2.25 million tonnes per annum, installation of two double strand slab casters and upgradation of the Hot Strip Mill.
The programme is being implemented through four global packages and 31 indigenous packages. And the work on the project is progressing as per schedule.
SAIL is also planning to install steel-making and slab casting facilities at its Salem Steel Plant as part of the steps toward backward integration.

The latest proposal is to have a process route consisting of an electric arc furnace, a combined top and side/bottom blown convertor for production of liquid steel and to have conventional slab caster or thin slab caster at Salem.

This facility would be used for production of stainless steel and other special steels and provisions will be kept in the layout for installation of VOD in future. This will take the capacity of the Salem Steel Plant to 421,000 tonnes of liquid steel per annum.
